title: Design an ATM (OOD)
prompt: Design an ATM. A customer inserts a card, authenticates with a PIN, then withdraws or deposits cash, checks balance, and takes their card back. Model the classes and, importantly, the ATM's state machine (card inserted, authenticated, transaction, dispensing). Show how cash is dispensed from the machine's bill denominations. Sketch the class diagram.
blurb: The State-pattern classic with a twist — model the ATM flow as states and solve cash dispensing across bill denominations.

rubric.label: Requirements clarification
rubric.description: Clarifies transaction types (withdraw/deposit/balance/transfer), auth flow, bill denominations, and whether the bank backend is in scope before designing.

rubric.label: Core entities
rubric.description: Identifies ATM, Card, Account, the State hierarchy, Transaction types, CashDispenser, and a BankService boundary.

rubric.label: State machine
rubric.description: A clean ATM state machine (Idle/CardInserted/Authenticated/SelectingTransaction/Dispensing) with well-defined transitions and per-state guards.

rubric.label: Class design
rubric.description: State as objects, CashDispenser separated, Transaction modeled polymorphically, no god ATM class with a mega-switch.

rubric.label: Cash dispensing
rubric.description: Dispenses an amount across denominations (greedy or Chain-of-Responsibility per bill), handles insufficient bills / non-dispensable amounts.

rubric.label: Design patterns
rubric.description: State for the flow, Chain-of-Responsibility for denomination dispensing, Strategy/polymorphism for transaction types; each justified.

rubric.label: API methods
rubric.description: insertCard, enterPin, selectTransaction, withdraw, deposit, ejectCard; routed through the current state.

rubric.label: Edge cases
rubric.description: Wrong PIN / lockout, insufficient funds, ATM out of cash, amount not dispensable, card left behind / timeout, cancel mid-flow.

rubric.label: Concurrency
rubric.description: Balance updates against the bank backend, avoiding double-debit; the ATM's cash inventory updated atomically with dispensing.

rubric.label: Extensibility
rubric.description: New transaction types, new denominations, multi-currency, or a new auth method slot in cleanly.

rubric.label: Communication
rubric.description: Draws the state diagram, walks a full withdrawal, and reasons about the dispensing and consistency edge cases.

functional_requirements: Read an inserted card and authenticate the customer via PIN
Offer transactions: withdraw, deposit, balance inquiry, (optional) transfer
Withdraw dispenses cash across available bill denominations and debits the account
Deposit accepts cash/check and credits the account
Eject the card and print/show a receipt; handle cancel at any step
Track the ATM's own cash inventory per denomination
nonfunctional_requirements: Deterministic flow via an explicit state machine
No double-debit; account update and cash dispense must be consistent
Fail safe: never dispense cash without a confirmed debit, and vice versa
Extensible transactions, denominations, and auth methods
Secure PIN handling and lockout on repeated failure
clarifying_questions: Which transactions — withdraw, deposit, balance, transfer?
Is the bank backend (account, balance) in scope or an external service we call?
What bill denominations does the machine stock?
PIN retry limit and lockout policy?
Do we handle card capture on timeout / left-behind card?

core_classes.name: ATM
core_classes.responsibility: Context: holds current State, the CashDispenser, the current session (card/account), and delegates each action to the state.

core_classes.name: ATMState (interface)
core_classes.responsibility: Encapsulates behavior for one step of the flow; illegal actions are guarded per state.

core_classes.name: IdleState / CardInsertedState / AuthenticatedState / SelectingTransactionState / DispensingState
core_classes.responsibility: Concrete states implementing only their legal transitions.

core_classes.name: Card
core_classes.responsibility: Card data: number, expiry, linked account reference; no PIN stored in clear.

core_classes.name: Account
core_classes.responsibility: Bank account balance operations (usually via BankService, not local).

core_classes.name: BankService (interface)
core_classes.responsibility: External boundary: authenticate PIN, check/debit/credit the real account atomically.

core_classes.name: Transaction (abstract) / WithdrawTxn, DepositTxn, BalanceTxn
core_classes.responsibility: Polymorphic transaction executed against the account; records amount and outcome.

core_classes.name: CashDispenser
core_classes.responsibility: Tracks bill inventory and computes/dispenses a payout across denominations.

relationships: ATM (Context) has-a current ATMState and delegates all actions to it
ATM composes a CashDispenser and holds a session (Card + Account)
ATM depends on BankService (interface) for real account operations
CashDispenser handlers can be chained per denomination (Chain of Responsibility)

design_patterns.why: Each step allows only its legal actions; replaces a fragile flag-based switch and prevents, e.g., withdrawing before auth.

design_patterns.where: CashDispenser as a chain of per-denomination handlers (100 -> 50 -> 20 -> 10)
design_patterns.why: Each handler dispenses as many of its bill as possible and passes the remainder down; adding a denomination is a new link.
Add transaction types without editing the ATM.
Isolate the ATM from the real banking backend and make it testable.

apis: boolean enterPin(String pin) — authenticates, with retry/lockout
void withdraw(int amount) — debits then dispenses
state_transitions: Idle --insertCard--> CardInserted --enterPin ok--> Authenticated; --pin fail x3--> Idle (card captured/ejected, locked)
SelectingTransaction --withdraw, funds ok, cash ok--> Dispensing --dispensed--> Authenticated (another txn?) / eject
Dispensing --insufficient funds / ATM out of cash / amount not dispensable--> SelectingTransaction (error, no debit)
edge_cases: Wrong PIN up to N times -> lockout / card capture
Insufficient account funds -> reject before dispensing
ATM out of cash or can't make the exact amount with stocked bills -> reject, no debit
Amount not a multiple of the smallest bill -> reject
Card left behind / user walks away -> timeout, capture or eject
Cancel mid-transaction -> unwind cleanly, eject card, no debit
Debit succeeds but dispense fails -> must reverse the debit (consistency)
concurrency: Withdraw must be atomic at the bank: debit and confirm before dispensing; use the BankService transaction so two ATMs/sessions can't double-spend the same balance

The critical consistency rule: never debit without dispensing and never dispense without a confirmed debit — order as reserve/debit -> dispense -> commit, with compensation (reverse debit) if dispense fails
ATM cash inventory decremented atomically with a successful dispense so a crash can't lose the count
PIN attempt counter per card guarded to prevent parallel brute force
extensibility: New transaction type (transfer, mini-statement): add a Transaction subtype — ATM/state flow unchanged
New denomination: add a link to the dispenser chain
Multi-currency: parameterize CashDispenser and amounts by Currency
New auth method (biometric, NFC): a new authenticate path behind BankService/AuthStrategy
Cardless/QR withdrawal: an alternate entry state feeding the same Authenticated flow

deep_dives.probe: Why model the flow as State objects rather than boolean flags and a switch? Show me what prevents a withdraw call before authentication in each approach.
Dispense $180 from 100/50/20/10 bills. How does your dispenser choose bills, what if it's out of 20s, and how do you detect a non-dispensable amount? Why Chain of Responsibility?
The account debits but the cash jams and doesn't come out. How do you avoid charging the customer — ordering, confirmation, and compensation?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions flag or boolean or switch on state
followup_bank.question: Boolean flags for authenticated/hasCard get tangled fast. How does the State pattern make illegal steps impossible, and what does adding a step cost?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions dispense or cash or bills
followup_bank.question: How do you break an amount into bills across denominations, and what happens when you're out of a denomination — greedy, or a Chain of Responsibility?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions debit or balance or withdraw
followup_bank.question: If the debit succeeds but the cash doesn't dispense, how do you keep the customer's balance correct — where's the compensation?
Where does PIN verification happen and how do you handle retries/lockout without storing the PIN on the ATM?

tradeoffs: State objects (safe, extensible) vs flags+switch (fewer classes, error-prone) — State wins as steps grow
Greedy dispensing (simple, may fail on odd stock) vs DP/exact bill selection (always finds a valid combo if one exists)
Debit-then-dispense with compensation (consistent, needs rollback) vs dispense-then-debit (risk of unpaid cash)
Thin ATM + BankService backend (testable, realistic) vs local Account (simpler, unrealistic)
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer models the ATM as a Context delegating to explicit State objects — Idle, CardInserted, Authenticated, SelectingTransaction, Dispensing — so each step permits only its legal actions and a withdraw-before-auth is structurally impossible rather than flag-checked. Transactions are polymorphic; a BankService interface is the boundary to the real account, keeping the ATM testable. Cash dispensing is a Chain of Responsibility over denominations (each handler dispenses what it can and passes the remainder), with explicit handling of out-of-a-denomination and non-dispensable amounts. The candidate nails the consistency rule — debit is confirmed before dispensing and a failed dispense reverses the debit — and covers wrong-PIN lockout, insufficient funds, out-of-cash, cancel/timeout, and atomic inventory decrement. They show the design extends to new transactions (subtype), denominations (chain link), multi-currency, and new auth methods without editing the state flow, and can justify State-vs-flags and greedy-vs-exact dispensing tradeoffs.

interviewer_notes: The centerpiece is the State pattern — if the candidate uses boolean flags (hasCard, isAuthenticated) and a switch, let them, then show how the flags tangle and ask what prevents withdraw before auth; steer to State objects. The second discriminator is cash dispensing: make them dispense a concrete amount, take a denomination out of stock, and force the non-dispensable case; reward Chain of Responsibility and anyone who notes greedy can fail where an exact combination exists. The senior-level probe is debit/dispense consistency — never debit without dispensing and vice versa, with compensation on failure. Keep the bank behind a BankService boundary; if they put balances locally, ask how a second ATM sees the same account. Over-engineering traps: building the whole banking backend, encryption ceremony, or a rules engine before the state flow works. If time remains, add a transfer transaction or a new denomination to test extensibility.
